index.title: Federation
index.lead: This service can be either end of a federation relationship, in five protocols: SAML 2.0, SAML 1.1, WS-Federation 1.2, OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0.
index.note: This is the one feature here that has to be configured before it will do anything. Everywhere else this service accepts what it is given — any username, any client_id, any entityID, any LDAP bind. It cannot do that here: what arrives at an assertion consumer service is an unauthenticated request claiming to be a person, and the session it produces is the one every other protocol in this process reads. So a relationship is created DISABLED, and an assertion is refused unless it verifies against the key configured on it.
index.consuming: Consuming: a foreign identity provider signs people in here
index.asserting: Asserting: this service signs people in to a foreign service provider
index.noConsuming: None configured. Add one in the console, or through POST /admin-api/federation/create.
index.noRelease: no release policy — this partner gets whatever /admin/claims and /admin/saml-attributes would give anybody
index.noAsserting: None configured. Every protocol endpoint here already issues to anybody that asks — what an identity-provider-side relationship adds is the partner being marked as a federation partner rather than a test client, and a list of which attributes are released to it.
index.loginPath: Start a federated sign-in. Takes ?returnTo=, a path on this service to land on afterwards.
index.acsPath: Where the answer comes back: the assertion consumer service, the WS-Federation wreply and the OAuth 2.0 redirect_uri, all one path. This is the URL to configure at the partner.
index.metadataPath: This service's own SAML metadata for that partner. Unsigned, deliberately.
index.sloPath: Where a partner's sign-out arrives in a browser: the SAML SingleLogoutService, the WS-Federation cleanup URL and the OpenID Connect post_logout_redirect_uri. It ends only the session the partner names, after the same signature check a sign-in gets.
index.backchannelPath: The OpenID Connect backchannel_logout_uri to register at the partner.
index.frontchannelPath: The OpenID Connect frontchannel_logout_uri to register at the partner, with frontchannel_logout_session_required.
index.base: The base URL this service sees itself at is {base}, so the URLs above are absolute from there.
index.buttonsOn: The sign-in screen offers every usable partner as a button.
index.buttonsOff: federation.loginButtons is off, so the sign-in screen offers no partner.
profile.title: A few details
profile.heading: A few details before your account is created
profile.lead: {partner} signed you in, but did not send everything this service needs to create your account. Give the details below to finish.
profile.note: These details are kept on your account here. An email address you type is recorded as unverified.
